goal: A worktree created outside scripts/susi-worktree.sh inherits the creating tree's susi.agent, so two worktrees answer to one identity and can renew, close and release each other's claims. It is live here: the primary checkout and a hand-made worktree under .claude/worktrees both carry PRIMARY, and a claim taken in one was attributable to both. The readiness board reports it but does not block it, and a report is not a guard. Refuse a commit from a worktree whose token another worktree also carries, name the offenders, and print the ordered fix - the claim has to be released and re-claimed because a claim travels with its token. STATUS: the script is written, proven three ways (a plain run; a run with GIT_DIR exported exactly as the hook sees it; a run from the PRIMARY-sharing worktree, which refuses and names the primary) and committed. Wiring it into .githooks/commit-msg is deliberately NOT done yet: doing so fails tests/hook_enforcement.rs in a quiet run, so that fixture asserts hook behaviour this guard changes. The remaining work is to understand that fixture - most likely it builds worktrees whose tokens are not unique, which the guard is right to refuse - and then wire the guard with the fixture corrected. The cause of two earlier failed attempts is recorded in the script: git exports GIT_DIR to hooks, so git -C <other worktree> reads this repository's config unless the inherited variables are unset.
title: One token per worker, enforced at commit time
